label: Python
headline: Python Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Python syntax and built-ins — variables, strings, lists, dicts, loops, functions, classes, file I/O, and more.

items.name: print()
items.definition: Output a value to the console.

items.name: Variables
items.definition: Store data without declaring a type — Python infers it automatically.

items.name: input()
items.definition: Read a string from the user via the console.

items.name: type()
items.definition: Return the data type of a variable.

items.name: Comment
items.definition: Single-line comment — Python ignores everything after the #.

items.name: Multiline comment
items.definition: Triple-quoted string used as a multiline comment or docstring.

items.name: str
items.definition: Text data. Use single or double quotes interchangeably.

items.name: int
items.definition: Whole numbers, positive or negative, with no decimal point.

items.name: float
items.definition: Numbers with a decimal point.

items.name: bool
items.definition: Boolean value — either True or False.

items.name: list
items.definition: Ordered, mutable sequence — items can be added, removed, or changed.

items.name: tuple
items.definition: Ordered, immutable sequence — cannot be changed after creation.

items.name: dict
items.definition: Key-value mapping — keys must be unique and hashable.

items.name: set
items.definition: Unordered collection of unique items.

items.name: int()
items.definition: Cast a value to an integer.

items.name: float()
items.definition: Cast a value to a float.

items.name: str()
items.definition: Cast a value to a string.

items.name: bool()
items.definition: Cast a value to a boolean. 0, None, empty string/list/dict are all False.

items.name: Addition
items.definition: Add two values.

items.name: Subtraction
items.definition: Subtract one value from another.

items.name: Multiplication
items.definition: Multiply two values.

items.name: Float division
items.definition: Divide and always return a float.

items.name: Integer division
items.definition: Divide and floor the result to an integer.

items.name: Modulo
items.definition: Return the remainder of a division.

items.name: Exponentiation
items.definition: Raise a number to a power.

items.name: Compound assignment
items.definition: Shorthand for counter = counter + 10. Works with -, *, /, // etc.

items.name: and
items.definition: True only if both a and b are truthy.

items.name: or
items.definition: True if at least one of a or b is truthy.

items.name: not
items.definition: Invert the boolean value of a.

items.name: is
items.definition: True if both variables point to the same object in memory.

items.name: Index access
items.syntax:
s[0]   # first char
s[-1]  # last char
items.definition: Access a character by position. Negative indices count from the end.

items.name: Slicing
items.definition: Extract a substring from index 2 up to (not including) index 5.

items.name: Slice from start
items.definition: Slice from the beginning up to index 3.

items.name: Slice to end
items.definition: Slice from index 2 to the end of the string.

items.name: Reverse string
items.definition: Return a reversed copy of the string using a -1 stride.

items.name: len()
items.definition: Return the number of characters in a string.

items.name: Concatenation
items.definition: Join two strings end to end.

items.name: Repeat
items.definition: Repeat a string n times.

items.name: in operator
items.definition: Test whether a substring exists inside a string.

items.name: Loop characters
items.definition: Iterate through each character in a string.

items.name: join()
items.definition: Concatenate a list of strings with a separator.

items.name: split()
items.definition: Split a string into a list on a delimiter.

items.name: strip()
items.definition: Remove leading and trailing whitespace.

items.name: replace()
items.definition: Return a copy of the string with a substring replaced.

items.name: lower() / upper()
items.definition: Convert all characters to lowercase or uppercase.

items.name: endswith()
items.definition: Return True if the string ends with the given suffix.

items.name: f-string (basic)
items.definition: Embed a variable directly in a string. Requires Python 3.6+.

items.name: f-string (expression)
items.definition: Evaluate any expression inside the curly braces.

items.name: f-string (decimals)
items.definition: Format a float to a fixed number of decimal places.

items.name: f-string (zero pad)
items.definition: Pad a number with leading zeros to a given total width.

items.name: f-string (thousands)
items.definition: Format a number with comma thousand separators.

items.name: f-string (percentage)
items.definition: Format a float as a percentage.

items.name: f-string (binary)
items.definition: Format an integer as a binary string.

items.name: f-string (hex)
items.definition: Format an integer as a lowercase hexadecimal string.

items.name: format() method
items.definition: Inject values into a string using positional placeholders.

items.name: % formatting
items.definition: Old-style string formatting using the % operator.

items.name: Create list
items.definition: Define a list with initial values.

items.name: From range
items.definition: Create a list of numbers from a range.

items.name: append()
items.definition: Add an element to the end of the list.

items.name: extend()
items.definition: Add all elements of another list to the end.

items.name: pop()
items.syntax:
li.pop()    # removes last
li.pop(0)  # removes first
items.definition: Remove and return an element by index (default: last).

items.name: del
items.definition: Delete an element at a specific index.

items.name: Index access
items.definition: Access an element by position. Negative indices count from the end.

items.name: Slicing
items.definition: Extract a sub-list using start:stop:step notation.

items.name: sort()
items.definition: Sort the list in place in ascending order.

items.name: reverse()
items.definition: Reverse the list in place.

items.name: count()
items.definition: Return the number of times a value appears in the list.

items.name: len()
items.definition: Return the number of elements in the list.

items.name: Repeat list
items.definition: Create a list by repeating elements n times.

items.name: List comprehension
items.syntax: [x**2 for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]
items.definition: Build a new list by applying an expression to each item, with optional filtering.

items.name: filter()
items.definition: Return only the elements for which the function returns True.

items.name: Tuple
items.definition: Ordered, immutable sequence. Cannot be modified after creation.

items.name: Tuple unpack
items.definition: Unpack tuple values into individual variables.

items.name: Set
items.definition: Unordered collection of unique items — duplicates are ignored.

items.name: set.add()
items.definition: Add a single element to the set.

items.name: set.remove()
items.definition: Remove an element from the set (raises KeyError if not found).

items.name: Union
items.definition: Return all unique elements from both sets.

items.name: Intersection
items.definition: Return only elements that appear in both sets.

items.name: Difference
items.definition: Return elements in s1 that are not in s2.

items.name: Create dict
items.definition: Define a dictionary with key-value pairs.

items.name: Access value
items.definition: Retrieve a value by its key. Raises KeyError if missing.

items.name: get()
items.definition: Retrieve a value by key, returning a default if the key doesn't exist.

items.name: Add / update
items.definition: Add a new key-value pair or overwrite an existing key.

items.name: update()
items.definition: Merge another dictionary into this one.

items.name: del key
items.definition: Remove a key-value pair from the dictionary.

items.name: keys()
items.definition: Return a view of all keys in the dictionary.

items.name: values()
items.definition: Return a view of all values in the dictionary.

items.name: items()
items.definition: Return a view of all (key, value) pairs.

items.name: Loop dict
items.syntax:
for k, v in d.items():
  print(k, v)
items.definition: Iterate over key-value pairs.

items.name: Dict comprehension
items.syntax: {k: v*2 for k, v in d.items()}
items.definition: Build a new dictionary using an expression over existing key-value pairs.

items.name: in operator
items.definition: Check whether a key exists in the dictionary.

items.name: if / elif / else
items.definition: Branch execution based on one or more conditions.

items.name: Ternary operator
items.definition: Assign a value based on a condition in a single line.

items.name: pass
items.definition: Do nothing — placeholder where a statement is syntactically required.

items.name: for loop
items.definition: Iterate over every item in an iterable.

items.name: while loop
items.definition: Repeat a block as long as a condition is true.

items.name: range()
items.definition: Generate a sequence of numbers with optional start, stop, and step.

items.name: enumerate()
items.definition: Loop with both the index and the value available.

items.name: zip()
items.syntax: for a, b in zip(list1, list2):
items.definition: Loop over two or more iterables in parallel.

items.name: break
items.definition: Exit the loop immediately.

items.name: continue
items.definition: Skip the rest of the current iteration and move to the next.

items.name: for / else
items.definition: The else block runs only if the loop finished without hitting a break.

items.name: Define function
items.definition: Define a reusable block of code that optionally returns a value.

items.name: Default argument
items.syntax:
def add(x, y=10):
  return x + y
items.definition: Provide a fallback value used when the argument is omitted.

items.name: *args
items.definition: Accept any number of positional arguments as a tuple.

items.name: **kwargs
items.definition: Accept any number of keyword arguments as a dictionary.

items.name: Multiple return
items.definition: Return a tuple and unpack it into separate variables.

items.name: Lambda
items.definition: A small anonymous function defined in a single expression.

items.name: map()
items.definition: Apply a function to every element of an iterable.

items.name: Define class
items.definition: Define a class with a constructor that initialises instance attributes.

items.name: Instantiate
items.definition: Create an instance of a class.

items.name: Method
items.definition: A function defined inside a class. self refers to the current instance.

items.name: Class variable
items.definition: A variable shared across all instances of the class.

items.name: Inheritance
items.definition: Create a subclass that inherits all attributes and methods from the parent.

items.name: super()
items.definition: Call a method from the parent class — commonly used in __init__.

items.name: __repr__()
items.definition: Define how the object is displayed as a string (e.g. in print or repr()).

items.name: Custom exception
items.definition: Create a custom exception type by inheriting from Exception.

items.name: Read file
items.syntax:
with open("file.txt", "r") as f:
  contents = f.read()
items.definition: Open a file and read its entire contents as a string.

items.name: Read line by line
items.definition: Iterate over each line without loading the whole file into memory.

items.name: Write file
items.definition: Write a string to a file, creating it if it doesn't exist.

items.name: Write JSON
items.syntax:
import json
with open("f.json", "w") as f:
  json.dump(data, f)
items.definition: Serialise a Python object to a JSON file.

items.name: Read JSON
items.syntax:
with open("f.json") as f:
  data = json.load(f)
items.definition: Deserialise a JSON file back into a Python object.

items.name: Delete file
items.definition: Delete a file from the filesystem.

items.name: Check file exists
items.definition: Safely check if a file exists before acting on it.

items.name: import
items.definition: Import an entire module and access its members with dot notation.

items.name: from import
items.definition: Import specific names from a module directly into the current namespace.

items.name: import as
items.definition: Import a module under a shorter alias.

items.name: dir()
items.definition: List all attributes and functions available in a module.

items.name: try / except
items.definition: Catch a specific exception and handle it gracefully.

items.name: Multiple exceptions
items.definition: Handle several exception types with a single except clause.

items.name: else clause
items.definition: Execute this block only if no exception was raised in try.

items.name: finally clause
items.definition: Always execute this block — used for cleanup like closing files.

items.name: raise
items.definition: Manually trigger an exception.

items.name: Generator function
items.definition: Use yield to produce values lazily one at a time instead of building a full list.

items.name: Generator expression
items.definition: Compact lazy generator — like a list comprehension but uses parentheses.

items.name: heapq (min-heap)
items.syntax:
import heapq
heapq.heapify(lst)
heapq.heappush(lst, 5)
smallest = heapq.heappop(lst)
items.definition: Turn a list into a min-heap. Push and pop maintain the heap property in O(log n).

items.name: deque
items.syntax:
from collections import deque
q = deque([1,2,3])
q.appendleft(0)
q.popleft()
items.definition: Double-ended queue with O(1) appends and pops from both ends — good for stacks and queues.

items.name: enumerate (start)
items.syntax:
for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
  print(i, line)
items.definition: Loop with a counter that can start at any number.
